subject: biology
title: Transpiration and stomata
key_idea: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from the leaves, through the stomata. It pulls water up the xylem from the roots. Guard cells open and close the stomata, which controls gas exchange and water loss.

blocks.text: Water travels from the soil to the air through the plant. This movement is called the transpiration stream.

items.meaning: The loss of water vapour from a plant, mainly through the stomata of the leaves.
Pores in the leaf surface, mostly in the lower epidermis. One is called a stoma.

diagram.alt: Put the journey of water through a plant in order, from the soil to the air.
diagram.prompt: Put the journey of water in order
steps: Water is absorbed from the soil by osmosis through the root hair cells
Water moves into the xylem in the root
Water travels up the xylem to the leaves
Water evaporates from the surface of the cells in the leaf
Water vapour is lost through the stomata to the air

items: Mineral ions dissolved in the water move up the xylem too.
Evaporation from the leaves pulls more water up the xylem, so water flows in one direction only.
Xylem is made of hollow tubes strengthened with lignin. It carries water and mineral ions up the plant.
Phloem carries sugars, not the transpiration stream.
Water goes: root hair cells, xylem, leaves, stomata, air.
Evaporation from the leaves drives the transpiration stream.
Water moves in one direction in the xylem.

blocks.text: Stomata have two jobs. Each stoma is surrounded by a pair of guard cells that open and close it.

items: Stomata allow gas exchange: carbon dioxide in and oxygen out.
Stomata allow water vapour to leave, which is transpiration.
Most stomata are in the lower epidermis, which reduces water loss.
A water lily has stomata only on its upper surface. The lower surface is in water, not air.

blocks.text: How guard cells open a stoma

diagram.alt: How a stoma opens. Guard cells photosynthesise and make glucose. Water enters the guard cells by osmosis. They swell and become turgid. The thicker inner wall bends less than the outer wall, so the cells curve and the stoma opens.
steps: Guard cells photosynthesise and make glucose
Water enters the guard cells by osmosis
Guard cells swell and become turgid
Thicker inner wall bends less than the outer wall
Cells curve and the stoma opens

items: At night, or when it is cooler or there is less light, the stomata are almost closed.
When guard cells lose water they become flaccid and the stoma closes.
Less water is lost when the stomata are closed.
Stomata allow gas exchange and water loss.
Guard cells take in water by osmosis, swell, curve and open the stoma.
Stomata are almost closed at night, so less water is lost.

checks.q: Describe the transport of water through a plant from the roots to the atmosphere.
checks.a: Water is transported in the xylem. It evaporates from the leaves. It is lost through the stomata.

checks.q: Describe how guard cells open a stoma.
checks.a: Water enters the guard cells by osmosis. The cells swell, become turgid and curve, which opens the stoma.
They allow gas exchange of carbon dioxide and oxygen. They allow water to evaporate from the leaf, which helps transpiration.

worked_example.question: This question is about plant transport systems. Describe how water is transported from the soil to the atmosphere through a plant.
answer_points: Water is absorbed from the soil by osmosis through the root hair cells.
It travels through the xylem to the leaves.
It is lost through the stomata to the atmosphere.
The process is driven by evaporation or transpiration.
worked_example.tip: Each step is one mark. "Evaporation" or "transpiration" alone is ignored: name where it happens.

worked_example.question: A student observed that the stomata were open. Describe how stomata open.
answer_points: The guard cells become turgid, change shape or swell.
Uneven thickness of the guard cell walls leads to bulging.
worked_example.tip: Any three points score one mark each.

worked_example.question: Explain how guard cells change shape to open stomata.
answer_points: Water enters the guard cells by osmosis.
The guard cells swell or become turgid.
The thickened inner part of the wall bends less than the outer part.
The guard cells curve, forming an opening.
worked_example.tip: Any four points score one mark each.
